one_liner: Go web server and reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS; claimed to beat nginx, but measured 4-14x slower in HttpArena.
what_it_does: Caddy is an HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server and reverse proxy written in Go. It is configured with a Caddyfile or native JSON, can be reconfigured live through an admin API, and obtains and renews TLS certificates on its own through CertMagic (ACME with Let's Encrypt or ZeroSSL, plus a local CA for internal names). Extra handlers are Go modules compiled in with xcaddy. It replaces nginx at the deployment level, not as a library: the config language, module API and directives are all different.
how_it_is_fast: No opened measurement shows it beating nginx; it is catalogued as a refuted claim. Its request path is Go's net/http (one goroutine per connection on the runtime's epoll netpoller), crypto/tls and quic-go. reverse_proxy reuses pooled upstream connections by default (http.Transport, MaxIdleConnsPerHost 32, 2-minute idle timeout), copies bodies through a sync.Pool of 32 KiB buffers, and streams responses instead of buffering them; automaxprocs and automemlimit fit GOMAXPROCS and GOMEMLIMIT to container limits. In HttpArena its custom-handler rows land at 0.64x (pipelined) to 1.40x (limited-conn) of a plain Go net/http server (go-stdlib; baseline-4096 0.86x), so its ceiling is net/http's per-request cost, not Caddy's middleware (derived from page data).
when_to_use: Many hostnames that need certificates issued and renewed automatically (ACME, on-demand TLS, internal CA), where operational simplicity matters more than peak requests per second.

TLS termination and reverse proxying in front of application servers at moderate load, where the upstream dominates latency; at a fixed 500 req/s the only same-workload test had nginx ahead by 14-23% on mean latency, which is small next to typical app latency.
Deployments that want HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 on by default (protocols h1 h2 h3) and Encrypted ClientHello without extra configuration.
Teams that prefer extending the server in memory-safe Go modules and changing config through a JSON API rather than C modules, Lua and reloads.
when_not_to_use: Edge or proxy tiers sized for maximum throughput per core: HttpArena baseline-4096 431,894 req/s against nginx 3,284,513 (0.13x), json-tls-4096 0.25x, baseline-h3-64 0.07x (derived from page data).
Tail-latency-sensitive services at high connection counts: HttpArena p99 113.50 ms vs nginx 6.79 ms on baseline-4096 and 1.99 s vs 52.31 ms on json-tls-4096.
Static files over HTTP/3 under load: static-h3-64 reached 22,218 req/s at 897% CPU against nginx's 361,025, so the QUIC path was the bottleneck rather than the cores.
Pipelined HTTP/1.1 clients: Go's net/http answers pipelined requests one at a time per connection (pipelined-4096 761,137 vs nginx 4,037,345 req/s).
Setups that depend on nginx.conf, njs or OpenResty Lua modules, since none of them carry over.

integration.form: standalone server binary; also a Go module (github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2) for plugins built with xcaddy
integration.dependencies: none at run time (static Go binary, no libc per the README); built on certmagic, quic-go, zap, klauspost/compress, automaxprocs and automemlimit
integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.26.0 to build from source (README and go.mod)
integration.platforms: Any OS and architecture Go targets; prebuilt binaries on GitHub Releases
integration.thread_safety: Not applicable as a library. Each request runs on its own goroutine, so custom handler modules must be safe for concurrent use.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces nginx as a TLS terminator, static server and reverse proxy at the deployment level, but needs a rewritten config (Caddyfile or JSON) and has no nginx module compatibility

gotchas: Harness flaw in the benchmark_url test, in every run: Vegeta sends HTTP/2 when the server offers it (-http2 defaults to true), Caddy offers h2 by ALPN by default, and the nginx server block is 'listen 443 ssl' without http2. So Caddy was measured over HTTP/2 and nginx over HTTP/1.1. The nginx upstream block also has no 'keepalive' directive, so nginx opened a new TCP connection to the backend for each request while Caddy reused pooled ones. Both asymmetries favour Caddy, and the tuned nginx still won.

The one Caddy win (256K mean 1.310211 ms vs 1.536594 ms) used the first nginx.conf (commit 0b7fd55). That config had worker_connections 1024, access logging on and no proxy_http_version, so nginx proxied over HTTP/1.0. Neither config sets proxy_buffers, so nginx proxied the 256 KiB body through its default buffers (8 x 4k/8k), which can spill to a temporary file.

The HttpArena Caddy rows are stale: Caddy v2.8.4 built on golang:1.22 with xcaddy, while the go-stdlib row uses Go 1.26 and Caddy is now at v2.11.7 (2026-10-03). v2.11.6 cut allocations in the request hot path and in reverse_proxy, and v2.11.7 roughly halved per-handshake certificate lookup time. Even so, plain net/http on Go 1.26 reaches only 504,598 req/s on baseline-4096, about 0.15x of nginx.

GC pauses: commenters on the Tyblog Caddy-vs-nginx benchmark reported latency spikes during Go garbage collection, while nginx stayed under 32 MB (search snippet only). In HttpArena Caddy used less memory than nginx's tuned build (80 MiB to 2.3 GiB vs 3.5 to 3.8 GiB), so memory results depend on the configuration.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Caddy over Traefik, the other Go reverse proxy here, when you configure by file or JSON and want automatic HTTPS with a local CA rather than container-label discovery. For raw proxy throughput neither is the pick: nginx itself, or routez and rproxy, which publish reverse-proxy numbers ahead of nginx, are the candidates to test.
verified_claims_summary: No opened measurement shows Caddy beating a configured nginx; the '4x' exists only as an HN title. In one Vegeta run (fixed 500 req/s, HTTPS reverse proxy to a local container, i7-10710U laptop, unpinned caddy:latest and nginx:latest), nginx had 14% lower mean latency on a 20-byte reply and, once its config was tuned, 23% lower on a 256 KiB body; Caddy's only win (1.17x) was against the untuned config. HttpArena (Threadripper PRO 3995WX, 32 cores and 64 threads for the server) puts Caddy v2.8.4 as an origin server at 0.07x to 0.25x of nginx 1.31.4's requests per second; nginx there is built at -O3 -march=native with a C handler module.
status_note: Very active (v2.11.7 released 2026-10-03, last commit 2026-10-10, 77.8k stars, 198 open issues) and Apache-2.0; a production-grade server, but listed here as a refuted speed claim rather than as a faster nginx.
